result.rationale: Verified in the office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts diff: the console.error of tokenResponse.error and the raw Microsoft responseJson is deleted and replaced by parseRefreshTokenResponse, which throws only the generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. judged_text: The refactor replaced refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse plus a console.error of the zod error and the raw Microsoft response with a helper that throws the generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', deleting the only diagnostics on this path. When Microsoft changes its token response fields (the historically flaky case this logging existed for), operators get a message with no field-level error and no record of responseJson, turning a five-minute diagnosis into a blind outage investigation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous logic did `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and, on failure, `console.error(...)` including both the Zod error and the raw `responseJson`. The refactor replaces this with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, whose implementation throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when parsing fails and does not log either the schema error details or `responseJson`. This concretely removes the only diagnostics on this failure path, matching the finding.
